component.name: Beisl
component.summary: Find out what made a game stutter

description.p: Beisl records what a game was actually doing when it stuttered. It wraps a launch, captures frametimes alongside CPU samples, and attributes each slow frame to a layer: the game itself, Wine, DXVK or vkd3d, the graphics driver, or the kernel. The answer is a split you can read, not a flame graph you have to interpret.
It is wine-agnostic. The same wrapper works under Steam with Proton, under Lutris or Heroic, or on a bare wine prefix, and it reads the environment rather than changing it.
Beisl also notices when a game cannot run at all:

ul.li: a vendor kernel anti-cheat no Wine can load
an unimplemented Wine function the game called

description.p: When that happens it says so while the game is still open, and hands the evidence to gamebus, where you can review it and file a report upstream yourself. Nothing is ever submitted for you.
Traces now know when a game hits a wall, the session window says so while it happens, and a new window hands every wall to gamebus for reporting.
The trace library grew an honest account of itself, and the setup app joined COSMIC 1.3.
First release: the wrapper, symbol resolution, the GUI and the MCP server.
